newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Cold and windy weather hits.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Cold and windy weather hits.

text.p: Cold temperatures and gusty winds arrived in the southern and central U.S. Plains late Monday, dealers in Kansas and Oklahoma said Tuesday.
Most merchandisers said temperatures were expected to only hit a high somewhere in the 20s (degrees Fahrenheit) Tuesday.
The cold helped slow movement somewhat, but dealers said they were not too worried about damage to the wheat crop.

"It wasn't like we were 70 degrees one day and then 20 the next," a dealer in south central Kansas said. "We did have a gradual temperature decline over the weekend, so this will be less of a shock to the wheat."
Meanwhile, merchandisers said Farmland Grain had posted steep discounts on lower-grade wheat at its terminal location in Enid, Okla.
Dealers said number three wheat was subject to a 20-cent- per-bushel discount. Number four was being hit with a 40-cent discount and number five was subject to a 70-cent discount.
"Something's going on," another Oklahoma dealer said. "It's apparent that they don't want anything bad."
Meanwhile, most dealers reported a lack of selling and basis levels were mostly unchanged, although one exporter at the Gulf lowered its bid significantly.
